page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor with 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, utilizing hyper-threading with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 1920 GB NVMe SSD. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show strong performance across several metrics. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the top tier, though multi-core performance falls into the average category, likely reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory performance is highly competitive, with large block write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores reaching the top tier. Cryptographic and compression capabilities are also robust, with single-threaded gzip and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top tier. For database workloads, the server demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations and PassMark database benchmarks. Large language model inference speeds are notable, with text generation for small and medium models reaching top-tier speeds.

The primary tradeoff of this server configuration is its shared CPU allocation, which can introduce resource contention and explains the average multi-core benchmark results despite the high vCPU count. However, the inclusion of a large 1920 GB NVMe SSD and 128.0 GB of RAM offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. This server is well-suited for database hosting, static web serving, large-scale file processing, and moderate LLM inference tasks.
